criterion_notes.c1: Examines household direct access to piped water across Mexican municipalities (proportion of households with a piped water network connection inside the dwelling).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 because it analyses intergovernmental fiscal transfers (Aportaciones Federales) and electoral patronage/governance dynamics in decentralized municipal water infrastructure funding (plain=yes). Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading because the analysed exposures are municipal indigenous population share and aggregate central-to-municipal per-capita fiscal transfers (covering infrastructure, health, education, and other programmes) driving physical network expansion, rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household service access such as eligibility rules, documentation/tenure requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, street-level discretion, or utility ownership/regulatory structure (narrow=no). Footnote mentions of 1990s privatisation reforms and Chiapas land-use law are background citations only and are not empirically analysed.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical study using municipal-level census, economic census, and public finance datasets (INEGI 1999, 2000, 2005) analysed via generalised linear models (GLM with logit link) and spatial-lag OLS regressions across 2,342 to 2,372 municipalities.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal-level piped water coverage in 2005 (share of households with a connection to the water network inside the dwelling).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies unit of analysis and sample (Mexican municipalities, N=2,372 in Model 1; N=2,342 in Models 2 and 3), exposures (indigenous population share in 2000 and cumulative per-capita federal transfers Aportaciones Federales 2000-2005), outcome (2005 municipal share of households connected to piped water inside the dwelling), and study design (observational longitudinal/cross-sectional municipal regression analysis).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in English.

study_design: Quantitative observational municipal-level regression study (generalised linear models with logit link and ordinary least squares regressions with spatial lags and state fixed effects using 1999-2005 census and public finance data).
population_and_sample: Mexican municipalities (unit of analysis: municipality; N = 2,372 municipalities in Model 1 and N = 2,342 municipalities in Models 2 and 3, out of 2,454 municipalities in Mexico).
exposure: Municipal indigenous population share (share speaking an indigenous language in 2000) and cumulative per-capita federal fiscal transfers to municipalities (Aportaciones Federales, 2000-2005), alongside presidential vote share, population density, per-capita income, and migration.
outcome: Municipal piped water coverage in 2005 (share of households in a municipality directly connected to the water network inside the dwelling) and per-capita federal transfers (2000-2005).
rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification of Criterion 2. While the paper empirically examines municipal household piped water coverage in Mexico (2000-2005) and would qualify under the broad/plain wording of Criterion 2 via its analysis of intergovernmental fiscal transfers (Aportaciones Federales) and political patronage, it investigates macro-fiscal infrastructure funding allocations and demographic/ethnic disparities in physical network expansion rather than a rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility criteria, tenure/documentation rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, enforcement, administrative burden, or utility ownership/regulation).
